p.src: Overview: We begin with the qualitative meaning of uncertainty. Two observables can be definite together only when they possess a complete common eigenbasis, and this is equivalent to their operators commuting. We then review unitary evolution and the Schrödinger equation, compare commutators with classical Poisson brackets, solve the time-dependent equation in the energy basis, and apply the result to a spin in a magnetic field. The final calculation gives precession of the spin expectation values, the two energy levels of a general spin Hamiltonian, and the distinction between a sideways expectation value and a photon of half the energy gap.

First we should finish the one-spin problem and put the ideas of uncertainty and time evolution on firmer ground.

Measurement generally changes the state and interrupts this isolated evolution.

The standard phrase expectation value means a statistical average. For an observable $L$, $\expect{L}(t)=\bra{\psi(t)}L\ket{\psi(t)}.$ Only the state vectors carry time dependence at this stage. Differentiating both sides and using Equation [eq:l5-schrodinger] together with its Hermitian conjugate, $\frac{d}{dt}\ket{\psi}=-iH\ket{\psi},
\qquad
\frac{d}{dt}\bra{\psi}=i\bra{\psi}H,$ gives $\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dt}\expect{L}
&=i\bra{\psi}HL\ket{\psi}
  -i\bra{\psi}LH\ket{\psi}\\
&=-i\expect{[L,H]}.
\end{aligned}$

Assume the energy eigenvalue problem has been solved. Expand an arbitrary state in the fixed energy basis: $\ket{\psi(t)}=\sum_j\alpha_j(t)\ket{E_j}.$ The basis vectors do not change in this description; all time dependence lies in the coefficients. Substituting Equation [eq:l5-energy-expansion] into Equation [eq:l5-schrodinger] gives $\begin{aligned}\sum_j\dot\alpha_j(t)\ket{E_j}
&=-i\sum_j\alpha_j(t)H\ket{E_j}\\
&=-i\sum_j E_j\alpha_j(t)\ket{E_j}.\end{aligned}$ Uniqueness of the expansion in a basis implies, for each fixed $j$, $\dot\alpha_j(t)=-iE_j\alpha_j(t),
\qquad\text{no sum on \(j\)}.$ The solution is $\alpha_j(t)=\alpha_j(0)e^{-iE_jt}.$

\sigma_x&=
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\\[0.4em]
\sigma_y&=

\sigma_z&=

\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}

-
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\\

\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}
-
\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\\
&=2
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}

[\sigma_x,\sigma_y]&=2i\sigma_z,\\
[\sigma_y,\sigma_z]&=2i\sigma_x.
\end{aligned}$ Reversing either entry reverses the sign.

p.src:
Every Hermitian $2\times2$ matrix can be expanded as $H=aI+b_x\sigma_x+b_y\sigma_y+b_z\sigma_z,$ with real coefficients. The identity term changes only the overall phase. The three remaining coefficients can be regarded as the components of a vector. Writing their magnitude as $\omega/2$ and their direction as a unit vector $\bm n$, the nontrivial Hamiltonian becomes $H=\frac{\omega}{2}\,\bm\sigma\cdot\bm n,
\qquad
\bm\sigma\cdot\bm n
=n_x\sigma_x+n_y\sigma_y+n_z\sigma_z.$ If $\bm B=B\bm n$, then $\bm n$ carries the direction of the field while $\omega$ carries its magnitude together with the magnetic coupling. It is $\bm n$, not $\omega$, that records orientation.

ja: これで単一スピンの非自明な時間に依存しない力学を使い尽くした。最初に不確定性を告げたのと同じ代数がその運動も生み出す。すなわち、非可換なパウリ行列がハミルトニアンを歳差運動に変え、ハミルトニアンと可換な成分は保存されたままである。次なる複雑さの増大は、別の1スピンのハミルトニアンではなく、独立な系を合成しもつれさせることができるより大きな状態空間である。
zh: 我们现在已经穷尽了单个自旋的非平凡时间无关动力学。最初预示不确定性的同一套代数也生成了它的运动：不对易的泡利矩阵将哈密顿量变成进动，而与哈密顿量对易的分量保持守恒。复杂性的下一次增加不是另一个单自旋哈密顿量，而是更大的态空间，在那里独立的系统可以被组合和纠缠。
